title: US to Offer $4 Billion Loan for Vistra to Boost Nuclear Output
key_facts: Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter who were not authorized to speak on record, that the Trump administration plans to offer Vistra Corp. a loan package of roughly $4 billion.
The money would upgrade three Vistra nuclear plants: two in Ohio and one in Pennsylvania.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright is expected to announce the funding as soon as Monday, during a planned visit to the Perry nuclear complex northeast of Cleveland.
Neither the Energy Department nor Vistra immediately returned messages seeking comment.
The size of the expansions Vistra plans was not immediately known.
Context from the article: data centers are driving a fast rise in electricity demand; Trump has set a goal of quadrupling US nuclear capacity by 2050.
Upgrading existing plants is one of the few ways to add capacity relatively quickly, because permitting and building new reactors takes long and costs a lot.
Vistra supplies the PJM grid, which runs from Illinois to Washington, DC, serves about 67 million people and is struggling to meet data center demand.
quote_evidence: The Trump administration plans to offer a roughly $4-billion loan package to Vistra Corp. to upgrade three of its nuclear plants, according to people familiar the matter.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright is expected to announce the funding as soon as Monday during a planned visit to the Perry nuclear complex northeast of Cleveland.
Both the Energy Department and Vistra didn't immediately return messages seeking comment.
why_it_matters_hint: A federal loan could add nuclear output at existing plants on a grid that is short of power for data centers, but it is not yet announced.
event_date: Report of 2 Oct 2026; announcement expected as soon as Monday 5 Oct 2026
notes: Single outlet (Bloomberg) with unnamed sources; no comment from the Energy Department or Vistra. Read on Yahoo Finance, which carries the Bloomberg text.
